Issue Number: close #28743, close #32160

Problem Summary:

### What is changed and how it works?

Due to the impact of new-collation, in `LogicalProjection.PredicatePushDown` some predicates not from the underlying operator are still pushed down, which causes some errors.
This PR lets it check whether a predicate is from the underlying operator before pushing it down.

issue_context.title: Selection on merge join could not find column
comments:
The problem happens when PDD(predicate-push-down) optimizer trying to substitute `a.abc` in where clause with `ifnull(t2.b,t1.a)`, for example:
```sql
select * from (select ifnull(t2.b,t1.a) abc from t1 left join t2 on t2.id=t1.id) a where a.abc >='2022-02-07 00:00:00';
```
is optimized to
```sql
select * from (select ifnull(t2.b,t1.a) from t1 left join t2 on t2.id=t1.id where ifnull(t2.b,t1.a) >= '2022-02-07 00:00:00') tmp;
```

When the new collation is enabled, the strictness of the collation should be also considered before the substitution(See `checkCollationStrictness`). Because the derived charset of `ifnull([datetime], [datetime])` is `utf8mb4` instead of `binary`, this check does not passed. Thus, the substitution is failed. However, this failure is not aware by PDD optimizer, the predicate is still pushed down.

https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/pull/30967 solves this problem.

review_comments: Any clearer comment why the `t2.b > 'a'` doesn't match the newly added `ExprFromSchema`?

Because the Projection creates a new column named `Column#7` to present `'a' collate utf8mb4_unicode_ci`, and `Column#7` cannot be substituted in `ColumnSubstitute`([L268](https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/blob/master/expression/util.go#L268)).
So if we push `Column#7` down, the underlying operators cannot recognize it when `ResolveIndex`.
This check seems horrible that may cause many regressions, but actually it only affects columns with specified collation.
Do you have any suggestions about this issue? @winoros @xuyifangreeneyes

Oh, after i go through the codes.
I found that the `ColumnSubsititute` might fail when correlation is enabled.
We can use `ColumnSubstituteImpl` to get the bool value which tells us whether the expr's substitution success.
I'll try to remove this logic(It might substitute fail) in the future.
